A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPECIAL and the same central FDIL research. Their complete main texts and Appendices A-F are readable and support matching equations, experiments and displays despite the changed title and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy, backward-transfer, runtime and sensitivity experiments on Digit-10, VLCS, PACS and DN4IL in Tables 1-2 and Figures 2-4.

after.justification: v2 retains original vision experiments and adds language, class-incremental, participation-rate and memory measurements, including Tables 4 and 14-30.

M1.justification: The core FDIL server-proximal update and Algorithms 1-2 are unchanged. Appendix F.6 adds a class-incremental adaptation described as dynamically expanding and adjusting classifier layers as new classes arrive.

E1.justification: Beyond the four retained vision benchmarks, v2 evaluates a GLUE sequence comprising SST-2, QQP and QNLI, and Split CIFAR-100 with five 20-class tasks. These add language coverage and class-incremental task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds FedAvg and FedProx to the main accuracy/BWT and runtime comparisons, introducing direct conventional-FL controls for the server-anchor contribution. All six original comparison methods remain; the language experiment separately uses the applicable replay-free methods and these FL controls.

E3.justification: New protocols include N = 2, 6 and 8 participation sweeps, DistilBERT with AdamW and alpha = 1 for language tasks, and five-task class-incremental evaluation. Worst earlier-task accuracy drop and memory measurements are added. The reported DN4IL lambda changes from 0.15 to 0.10. PACS rounds are inconsistent within v2: Table 6 lists 20, while Section 5 and Appendix F.2 retain 30; this does not establish a coherent budget revision.

E4.justification: v2 adds participation sensitivity, per-domain accuracy and worst-forgetting diagnostics, SPECIAL-C lambda sensitivity, and client/GPU memory comparisons. Figure 3 also revises the SPECIAL lambda sweep. The existing T, E and alpha ablation and Figure 4 are retained and moved to Appendix F.4, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions specify the same three seeds, 25, 225 and 2025, and use the same mean-with-plus/minus reporting in their main comparisons. No new uncertainty estimator, confidence interval, significance test or increased run count is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive baseline, participation, per-task and memory results, plus language ACC/BWT of 74.70%/-4.03% and class-incremental results of 40.68%/-9.00%. Original SPECIAL Table 1 entries are retained, while SR-FDIL's reported VLCS ACC changes from 48.71% to 49.38%. Figure 3's plotted sweep values also change. These additions do not demonstrate a same-setting improvement of SPECIAL between versions.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 replaces the assertion that Eq. (3) is equivalent to the cumulative objective with the weaker characterization of a regularized surrogate. Section 5 also introduces the minimum earlier-task accuracy-drop definition. The main assumptions, BKT and convergence bounds, and Appendix C-E proofs otherwise remain substantively unchanged after renumbering.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a server-side proximal anchor with constant communication/model footprint, a backward-transfer bound, and task-uniform non-convex convergence under partial participation. The expanded experiments support these retained claims without redefining the principal theoretical contribution.

C2.justification: v2 corrects the underfitting explanation for favorable BWT from large to low initial-task accuracy, explains why FedAvg can achieve strong ACC while forgetting, and adds a local lambda-tolerance interpretation. Limitations acknowledge language evaluation and omit v1's explicit very-large-scale caveat. The central stability-plasticity explanation is retained.

D1.justification: New Tables 6-7 disclose dataset sizes, image dimensions and method-specific baseline hyperparameters. The added experiments supply selected backbone, optimizer, partition and task-split details. Most original learning-rate schedules, hardware, seed information and search procedures remain; no new code or data release is documented.

R1.justification: v2 adds explicit positioning against conventional-FL anchors while retaining the Appendix A survey and principal novelty comparisons. The MNIST database citation is replaced by a document-recognition paper. Most other reference changes are publication or bibliographic updates rather than newly introduced research.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, theoretical commentary and experimental discussion receive substantial rewriting. The title changes, terminology shifts from memory-free to replay-free, the original ablation discussion moves to the appendix, and a numbered Conclusion and Limitations section and expanded experimental appendix reorganize the narrative.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column formatting. Table 1 gains comparator groups and performance shading; numerous diagnostic and benchmark tables are added. Figure 3 changes from a horizontal four-panel display to a 2-by-2 arrangement, while Figure 4 is enlarged and relocated to the appendix. Figures 1-2 retain their underlying graphics.

improvement.justification: The added FedAvg/FedProx controls, participation sweeps and forgetting/memory diagnostics make the anchor's benefits and tradeoffs more assessable than in v1. Broader evaluations and clearer BWT interpretation also help. The net gain is limited by new reporting inconsistencies: PACS uses 20 versus 30 rounds in Table 6 and Section 5, and FedProx PACS ACC is 42.99% in Table 1 versus 37.99% in Table 11. These discrepancies weaken reproducibility and confidence in parts of the expanded evidence.
